editorial.description_en: Iron sand from a river bed — dark, cool, and metallic without being bright.
editorial.description_ja: 川底の砂鉄のような、暗く青みのある色。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.440, C 0.013, h 252.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 鉄 (tetsu, iron) + 砂 (suna, sand), reversing the ordinary word 砂鉄 (satetsu) rather than reusing it. It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Iron Sand" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 鉄砂. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — kumori-iwa at ΔE00 8.2, ame-iwa at ΔE00 8.9, yoru-giri at ΔE00 9.3. complementary is empty because at chroma 0.013 the hue is not a reliable enough statement to oppose. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
